questions.q: By default, what happens if a GitHub Actions status check on a PR fails, but no branch protection rule marks it as required?
options: The merge button is automatically disabled
The repository is automatically archived
The PR can still be merged — a non-required check is purely informational
GitHub emails the repo owner every hour
questions.explain: A status check that isn't marked required in a branch protection rule doesn't block anything — it's just a visible signal a reviewer can ignore.

questions.q: What does marking a status check "required" in a branch protection rule actually do?
options: It makes the check run faster
It removes the merge button's availability until that check passes
It automatically fixes any failures
It only applies to non-admin contributors
questions.explain: A required status check turns a passing CI run into a hard precondition for merging — the merge option becomes unavailable until it passes.

questions.q: What does `required_approving_review_count: 1` add to the gate, alongside the automated checks?
options: A second automated test run
A requirement that at least one human reviewer approve the PR before it can merge
A requirement that Slither run twice
A requirement for two separate branch protection rules
questions.explain: This setting requires a human approval in addition to passing automated checks — the two aren't redundant, since they catch different categories of problem.

questions.q: Why does the lesson argue a human reviewer still belongs in the gate, even with Slither and the full test suite required?
options: Because automated tools are always wrong
Because automated tools only catch known vulnerability patterns, not whether the business logic actually does what the spec intends
Because GitHub requires at least one human approval by law
Because human review is faster than running tests
questions.explain: Static analysis and tests catch known patterns and asserted behavior — they can't judge whether the actual business logic is correct, which is why a human reviewer stays in the required gate.

questions.q: What is the actual payoff of wiring up required status checks, according to this lesson?
options: CI runs become faster
"All tests pass and Slither is clean" becomes an enforced property of the repository itself, not a convention the team has to remember to follow
Developers no longer need to write tests
Gas costs are automatically reduced
questions.explain: The lesson's core point: enforcement by the platform (branch protection) beats enforcement by discipline (a team convention someone can forget or skip under pressure).
